question: Which hormones are mostly used in birth control drugs to prevent pregnancy?
explanation: Birth control pills use artificial forms of estrogen and progestin to change the body's hormone balance and stop pregnancy. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h1)

question: How do hormones in birth control pills mainly stop ovulation?

options.B: By blocking egg movement in the tube
options.C: By triggering a luteinizing hormone surge
options.D: By sending negative feedback to the pituitary gland

explanation: Steady levels of artificial hormones tell the brain to stop the hormone surges needed to release an egg. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h1)

question: Combined birth control pills contain which two active ingredients?

options.B: An estrogen and an oxytocic agent

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives mix artificial estrogen and progestin to work together against pregnancy. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h2)

question: Which action is shared by both combined and progestin-only birth control methods?

options.A: Thickening the cervical mucus to block sperm

explanation: The progestin found in both methods changes cervical fluids, making it hard for sperm to swim upward. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h2)

question: How often is Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA) given as an injection?
explanation: DMPA injections release progestin slowly over time, so patients need a new shot every 8 to 12 weeks. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h3)

question: What is a common effect of injectable progestins compared to daily birth control pills?

options.A: They do not enter the bloodstream
options.C: They contain high doses of estrogen
options.D: Ovulation may take longer to return after stopping

explanation: Depot injections stay in body tissues for a while, meaning normal cycles can take several months to restart after the last shot. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h3)

question: Why must progestin-only pills be taken at the exact same time every day?

options.B: They leave the body very quickly
options.C: They react with food in the stomach

explanation: Because progestin-only pills clear fast from the system, taking them on time keeps the cervical mucus thick and protective. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h4)

question: How do emergency contraceptive pills work after unprotected sex?

options.A: By destroying fertilized eggs in the uterus
options.B: By absorbing all sperm in the vagina
options.D: By delaying or stopping the release of an egg

explanation: Emergency pills work before fertilization by pushing back ovulation so sperm cannot meet an egg. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h4)

question: Which birth control method requires almost no daily action from the user after it is put in place?
explanation: LARCs like implants and IUDs offer continuous protection for years without needing daily pills or action before sex. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h5)

question: What is a major health benefit of barrier methods compared to hormonal birth control?

options.A: They protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.C: They require no special placement skill
options.D: They stop the menstrual cycle completely

explanation: Barrier methods physically block germs, making them unique in helping prevent both STIs and pregnancy. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h5)

question: What serious blood vessel problem is linked to the estrogen in combined birth control pills?
explanation: Estrogen increases liver production of clotting factors, which raises the risk of blood clots in the veins. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h6)

question: A patient taking a combined pill complains of frequent nausea and tender breasts. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Nausea and breast tenderness are common side effects linked to higher estrogen levels in combined pills. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h6)

question: Which condition means a patient should definitely NOT use combined hormonal contraceptives?
explanation: A past blood clot means the extra estrogen in combined contraceptives can cause dangerous repeat clotting. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h7)

question: How do drugs like rifampicin affect how well hormonal birth control works?

options.A: They bind to hormones in the gut and stop absorption
options.B: They turn progestin into a fertility booster
options.C: They break down hormones faster in the liver, lowering effectiveness
options.D: They make estrogen levels dangerously high

explanation: Certain medications make the liver clear contraceptive hormones from the blood too quickly, which can lead to accidental pregnancy. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h7)

question: What is an important duty of the nurse when assessing a new family planning patient?

options.C: Checking for medical conditions that make certain methods unsafe

explanation: Nurses must carefully review a patient's medical history to make sure the chosen birth control method is safe for them. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h8)

question: Why is culturally sensitive counseling very important in Nigerian family planning nursing practice?

options.A: It removes the need for a physical exam
options.C: It helps address local myths and rumors about modern methods
options.D: It stops patients from ever having side effects

explanation: Cultural beliefs and community stories can affect how patients use birth control, so respectful dialogue and education are essential. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h8)
